chunks: Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:
Earnest money is not permissible unless it is a cash portion of the price.

key_terms.الثَّمَنِ: the price of the sold item
key_terms.الْعَرَبُونُ: earnest money or down payment given in a sale transaction
key_terms.لَا يَجُوزُ: is not permissible or legally valid
key_terms.نَقْداً: in cash; as an immediate monetary payment

ai.seo_question: When is earnest money in a sale permissible according to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on al-ʿarabūn, or earnest money in a sale. It states that such a payment is only permissible when it is counted as an actual part of the purchase price, indicating a rule in commercial fiqh concerning valid sale conditions.
